thread.title: Amazon and Apple: Los Angeles is the ultimate HQ2 wild card

author: Mike Sunnucks
title: Amazon and Apple: Los Angeles is the ultimate HQ2 wild card
text: – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 19, 2018, 11:46am MST Updated Jan 19, 2018, 2:02pm MST Los Angeles Mayor Eric Garcetti posted a GIF of a celebrating Kermit the Frog on his Twitter (NYSE: TWTR) yesterday after his city was named one of the 20 finalists for a second headquarters for Amazon.com (Nasdaq: AMZN) Los Angeles and Denver were the only two Western markets to make the final cut for the $5 billion second headquarters for Seattle-based Amazon. Bids from Phoenix, Tucson, Tempe and Mesa didn’t get invited to the Amazon prom. Arizona bids lacked the big tax breaks and subsidies being offered by other states such as Pennsylvania, Maryland and New Jersey bidding for Amazon. “There is a laundry list of attributes that make this region stand out, but we were competing against more than 230 cities in North America, ranging in geographic location and some that offered very competitive incentive programs,” said Chris Camacho, president and CEO of the Greater Phoenix Economic Council . Amazon’s snub leaves Arizona economic developers and business recruiters focused on other fish in the sea. “While Greater Phoenix did not make the short list for this particular project, our team is diligently working with more than 300 domestic and international companies who are currently exploring metro Phoenix as an option for expansion or relocation,” Camacho said. “This market continues to be an attractive business destination.” That includes Apple Inc . (Nasdaq: AAPL). Apple is looking for a new campus with a customer support focus as part of its $350 billion U.S. investment effort. That move comes after tax cuts passed by President Donald Trump and Congress. Apple is repatriating $250 billion back to the U.S. and paying $38 billion at one time 15 percent rate (a provision part of the Trump tax cuts). National economic development and site selection expert John Boyd said Phoenix should be a strong contender for Apple. Phoenix and its suburbs are already home to large back-office operations for scores of companies including Paypal Holdings (Nasdaq: PYPL), Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC) and Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS). Apple already has a big data center in Mesa and likes Southwestern states with footprints also in Texas and Nevada. “Phoenix Community and Economic Development is aware of the Apple proposal,” said city spokesperson. “Phoenix has many of the assets needed for a major corporate campus and we welcome business prospects from all industries. For professional etiquette, our practice is to not comment about any possible pending proposals or reveal our competitive strategies.” Los Angeles is considered a long shot for landing the $5 billion Amazon second headquarters. Gur Jeff Holzmann, managing director of commercial real estate and site selection firm iintoo USA, said L.A. is too expensive compared to other markets. But other technology companies have liked the L.A. market for operations. It’s media hub and Amazon is in the realm too. Bezos has a house in Beverly Hills. He bought a neighbor’s there for $12.9 million to create a compound there. While, most site selectors peg Boston, New York, Atlanta or Austin as favorites for HQ2 because of their time zone diversity from Seattle, if Amazon has its sights set on Asia and the Chinese market where it competes with Alibaba (NYSE: BABA) and others then Los Angeles might be a more serious contender. – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 19, 2018, 11:46am MST Updated
